title: ElevenLabs Realtime Speech to Text for Voice Agents
summary: ElevenLabs realtime voice agents process speech instantly. Evaluate the latency and accuracy against your application's requirements.
body_markdown:
## Fix the Glue Work With Activepieces


Every connector is an agent tool.


Connect an integration once in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/elevenlabs) , and the same action serves two callers: it runs as a step in the post-call flow, and it is exposed as a tool on the project's MCP server, where Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent you built can call it, which means you avoid duplicating the integration.


The CRM update or ticket your agent needs after the transcript is therefore never integrated twice, and the shared mechanism lives under packages/integrations in the open source repo. It sits downstream of the ear and doesn't do anything for the delay you just measured.


The sequence matters. Speech ends, the transcript arrives, and then something has to record it somewhere.


Most teams hand-roll that step inside the process that holds the audio socket, so a slow CRM call or a failed ticket request shares a failure domain with the live conversation.


Moving it into a separate workflow means a broken integration fails in its own run history, where you can read it, instead of as dead air on a call.


On the canvas of the builder below sits a three-step flow: an Every Hour trigger, an Ask ChatGPT action, and an End node.


The open Select Step panel has "sheet" typed into its search field, and it returns[Microsoft Excel 365](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/microsoft-excel-365) , Google Sheets, AITable and Kimai, each with its own actions.


Take from it that every destination is a selectable integration, so adding a spreadsheet row is a pick from a list, not an SDK integration you maintain yourself.


The limits come next. We haven't run ElevenLabs realtime through Activepieces, and we've not confirmed a dated Activepieces release aimed at it, so we claim none.


Integration breadth doesn't show that this particular handoff works, so you must test this workflow in your actual environment.


Activepieces doesn't replace the ElevenLabs endpoint: it hears nothing and transcribes nothing. Treat it as the wiring after the ear.


Its core is MIT-licensed, so you can read how a step runs, and you should still test the handoff against your own transcript events before you trust it.
